data.name: Absolute Sol
data.detailed_description:
Absolute Sol is a living sandbox of our Solar System. You fly it, inspect it, and then start changing it.

Move Earth. Drop a moon inside a Roche limit. Hit a world with a probe or an asteroid. Time is yours — pause it, speed it up, or bake years ahead and watch climates, orbits, and surfaces respond.

This is a simulation first. The pictures should look good, but the point is that the system behaves like a system: heat, gravity, breakup, and the things you can read off a planet when you actually look.

What you can do now

  • Fly the Solar System — the Sun, the planets, major moons, rings, and belts, from a wide overview down to a single world. Default scale keeps inner worlds readable from the Sun; true physical scale is one toggle away.

  • Edit and create — change orbits, spin, mass, air, and water, or spawn new bodies and see what they do to everything else.

  • Watch Earth react — oceans, ice, atmosphere, weather, and surface damage as you move it, heat it, freeze it, or hit it.

  • Roche limits — push a moon or small body too close and watch it stretch and come apart into grit and debris.

  • Impacts — probes, asteroids, and collisions, with scars, debris, and secondary hits.

  • Science overlays — atmosphere layers, magnetosphere, ring profiles, and stellar heatmaps, with plain-language (i) tips on every inspector number. Built so a curious kid and a tired adult can both follow along.

  • Scenarios — guided starts: free play at today’s date, Apollo 11, a true-size lineup, a Goldilocks parade at 1 AU, a tide-locked Earth, or a look-only grand tour of the family.

  • Bake Studio — run the clock forward (orbits, belts, Roche drama, or climate) then play the result back. Compute once; watch at a human pace. A Research fidelity is there for classrooms that want denser steps.

  • Runs on more than a beast PC — Low / Medium / High / Ultra, optional surface shadows, and belt-density toggles (main belt, Trojans, Kuiper, and the rest) so a laptop can still fly the system.

  • Sandbox extras — a few toys for testing the system at scale, including a Superlaser Platform (our own constructed, moon-scale body).

What this is — and isn’t

Absolute Sol is Early Access. The Solar System is playable, the sandbox works, and development is daily. Visuals, effects, and tools will keep getting better. Scientific behavior stays the priority.

Buy it for what you can do today: sit in the system, break a rule, and see what happens.

data.short_description: A physics sandbox of our Solar System. Fly the planets, change orbits, and watch Earth freeze, boil, or take a hit. Spawn worlds, cross Roche limits, and inspect atmospheres, magnetospheres, rings, and stellar heatmaps.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: Windows 10 64-bit (version 1909 or later)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-8400 / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 or equivalent
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 1660 / AMD RX 5600 XT (6 GB VRAM) or equivalent
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Storage: 8 GB available space
  • Sound Card: DirectX compatible
  • Additional Notes: 1920×1080 recommended at Minimum. Lower Graphics (Low/Med) and avoid very high particle/belt counts for best performance.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: Windows 10/11 64-bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i7-10700 / AMD Ryzen 7 3700X or better
  • Memory: 32 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA RTX 3060 / AMD RX 7600 XT (16 GB) or better
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Storage: 8 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: 2560×1440 or 4K supported. High/Ultra and dense asteroid belts are GPU/CPU heavy
